claims.text: Low-dose supplementation with EPA-DHA does not significantly reduce the rate of major cardiovascular events among post-myocardial infarction patients receiving state-of-the-art medical therapy.
Low-dose supplementation with ALA does not significantly reduce the rate of major cardiovascular events among post-myocardial infarction patients receiving state-of-the-art medical therapy.
In a prespecified subgroup of women, ALA supplementation was associated with a reduction in major cardiovascular events that approached statistical significance.

evidence.description: Hazard ratio for major cardiovascular events with EPA-DHA was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.87 to 1.17; P=0.93).
Hazard ratio for major cardiovascular events with ALA was 0.91 (95% CI, 0.78 to 1.05; P=0.20).
In the prespecified subgroup of women, ALA compared with placebo and EPA-DHA alone yielded a hazard ratio of 0.73 (95% CI, 0.51 to 1.03; P=0.07).

methodologies.name: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial
methodologies.description: A 40-month randomized controlled trial testing the effect of trial margarines supplemented with EPA-DHA, ALA, both, or placebo on primary cardiovascular events.
conditions: 4837 patients aged 60 through 80 years with prior myocardial infarction
Concomitant state-of-the-art antihypertensive, antithrombotic, and lipid-modifying therapy
40 months duration of supplementation via daily margarine intake
Targeted daily intake: 400 mg EPA-DHA, 2 g ALA, or placebo
